question: Which statement best describes Actions & useActionState?
options: Reads the pending state of the nearest parent <form> from inside a child component — no prop-drilling a isPending down to your submit button.

Shows an expected result immediately while the real request is in flight, then reconciles with the confirmed state when it resolves (or reverts on error). This packages the manual 'add now, fix after await' pattern.

An Action is an async function you hand to React (via <form action={fn}> or a transition). React runs it as a transition and tracks its lifecycle for you. useActionState wraps an action and returns [state, dispatch, isPending] — the returned state is whatever your action returns (e.g. a validation error), so you get pending and error handling with zero manual flags.

use() unwraps a resource during render. For a promise it integrates with Suspense (the component suspends until it resolves); for context it replaces useContext and — unlike hooks — may be called conditionally or in a loop. The promise must be stable/cached, not created inline each render.
